question.text: Let $f(\theta)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & \cos \theta & -1 \\ -\sin \theta & 1 & -\cos \theta \\ -1 & \sin \theta & 1\end{array}\right|$. Suppose $A$ and $B$ are respectively maximum and minimum values of $f(\theta)$. Then $(A, B)$ is equal to

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & f(\theta)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & \cos \theta & -1 \\ -\sin \theta & 1 & -\cos \theta \\ -1 & \sin \theta & 1\end{array}\right| \text { (after expansion) } \\ & f(\theta)=1+\sin 2 \theta \\ & A=2, B=0 \quad(A, B)=(2,0)\end{aligned}$
